review.title: Corrective, re-run: unknown media metadata semantics under an honest review range
review.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0205 and carries the same implementation forward under a base that is actually true. PL-0205 recorded implementationBaseSha 18ce47244b1da0c83fe092351f51e71892bd6c84, derived mechanically as the first parent of the first commit that touched packages/contracts/src/shared/media-facts.ts. The derivation was honest and the answer was wrong, for a reason the probe file conceals: that file was CREATED by PL-AI-0006's module split, not by PL-0205. The split moved existing declarations out of packages/contracts/src/index.ts and states in its own commit that schema behaviour did not change -- so the parent tree of that creation ALREADY CONTAINED PL-0205's semantics. Required-and-nullable codecs, height and bitrate, MediaFact, MEDIA_FACTS, unknownMediaFacts and CompatibilityConfidence all exist in the old barrel. The recorded base therefore opens the review range AFTER the implementation it claims to cover, which is the same defect class as PL-0703's, arriving from the opposite direction. THE GENERAL LESSON, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LEARNED TWICE: the file that exists only for a task is not a safe provenance probe when a later refactor could have created that file by moving content into it. A file's creation date is the date of the FILE, not of the behaviour inside it. A probe must be chosen for when the BEHAVIOUR appeared, and the way to check that is to read the parent tree and confirm the behaviour is absent there. THE TRUE BASE IS cf2a4583e120151bf16e90d8eb41842cd7329c83, established by gpt-architect by reading the trees rather than the filenames: 4091a2b65b8f187ccb87a04790272007dabd39ea is the commit that introduced the semantics, its message names PL-0205 preflight work, and its parent cf2a4583 still has mandatory non-null codecs, height and bitrate and none of the unknown-media vocabulary. Claim this task, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base cf2a4583e120151bf16e90d8eb41842cd7329c83. Do NOT use 18ce4724, and do not attempt to repair PL-0205 in place: reconciliation refuses a task that already records a base, because reconciliation establishes a base rather than revises one, and release is unreachable from REVIEW and deliberately preserves the base anyway. PL-0205 is BLOCKED with its false derivation preserved as audit history.
review.notes: MERITS ALREADY APPROVED, PROVENANCE IS THE ONLY REASON THIS TASK EXISTS. gpt-architect reviewed the implementation on the merits at 98d18154655dbaaa6678ef261743f9971f106293 and found it approvable: unknown media facts are required-and-nullable so absence and unknown cannot be conflated, stated unsupported codecs are still rejected, unstated codecs remain only attemptable and explicitly unverified rather than being certified compatible, rights still precede every technical decision, and scoring gives an unknowable positive dimension zero credit without renormalising the ceiling, so a missing fact cannot become a fabricated favourable measurement. It declined to record that as a verdict on PL-0205, because a verdict bound to a false range is worth less than no verdict. ACCEPTANCE REWRITTEN ON THE REVIEWER'S EXPLICIT RULING, AND THE CODE WAS NOT TOUCHED. PL-0205's clause said eligibility must not PASS on an unverified codec, which is ambiguous enough to imply rejection; the implementation reads it as must not CERTIFY. Asked which way to resolve it, the reviewer chose the code: the three-state model is the better design, so an unstated codec must never be certified as supported but may remain attemptable as explicitly unverified, while a stated unsupported codec is rejected. That is what the acceptance below now says. This is the second acceptance corrected this round to match a reviewed architecture rather than the reverse, and both were the reviewer's instruction. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED AGAIN, ON A FINDING WORTH KEEPING. PL-0205 declared packages/media-engine/** and the reviewer refused it -- not on tidiness, but because allowedPaths is WRITE OWNERSHIP: the wildcard intentionally owned neighbouring PL-0202, PL-0203 and PL-0204 files this task never wrote, which is exactly why PL-0205's published window read 27 files. Its words: keeping a wildcard solely because the tasks are already serialized is the same reservation inflation you correctly removed from contracts. The verified media-engine write set is the five files below; 4091a2b introduced the first four and 79a0e651 added the property suite. THE THREE CONTRACTS LEAVES ARE THIS TASK'S CONTENT IN FILES ANOTHER TASK PLACED, and that is stated rather than hidden: shared/media-facts.ts, shared/codecs.ts and domains/playback.ts hold PL-0205's declarations, but PL-AI-0006's module split is what put them in those files. The content is reviewed here; the placement is reviewed there. PL-AI-0006 will legitimately declare the same paths when it is claimed, so the two must be sequenced rather than run together -- which packages/contracts already forces, since PL-AI-0006 declares the package wildcard. COLLISION-CHECKED: every entry below is a leaf file, prefix-disjoint in both directions from PL-0706's packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and runtime.test.ts, from PL-0105's apps/web and docs paths, and from PL-0204's packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. It DOES overlap PL-0204 and PL-0206, on packages/contracts/src/testing/arbitraries.ts exactly and on the media-engine leaves their packages/media-engine/** prefix-contains. That is honest rather than accidental: all three genuinely wrote arbitraries.ts, and declaring it on one alone would understate one review surface to flatter another. It costs nothing extra either, and the reason is the overlap itself rather than agent capacity -- conflictWithActive refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner, so PL-0204 and PL-0206 wait for this task on the files they share whatever claude-media's maxParallel is set to. That limit was raised from 1 to 2 this round for a different task entirely, PL-0601, whose surface is genuinely disjoint from this one.
review.acceptance: StreamCandidate can represent genuinely unknown videoCodec, audioCodec, height and bitrateKbps, and unknown must be ASSERTED rather than reached by silence: the four facts are required-and-nullable, so an explicit null parses, an omitted or undefined field is refused, and no numeric sentinel stands in for a measurement. The media engine then treats unknown as unknown rather than as a value. Eligibility must never CERTIFY an unstated codec as supported; such a candidate remains attemptable and is labelled explicitly unverified, while a STATED codec the device cannot decode is still rejected and a STATED height above the ceiling is still refused. Rights are checked before anything unknown can excuse a candidate. Scoring must neither award nor penalise a fabricated number: every unknowable dimension scores zero on a positive weight, the attainable ceiling is reported rather than used as a divisor, and nothing renormalises for what could not be measured.

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck via npm run check, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree committed this round. No code changed between PL-0205's gates and these: the four facts are still required-and-nullable so unknown must be asserted rather than reached by silence, and CODEC_EFFICIENCY is still keyed by VideoCodec rather than by the candidate field so a null cannot index it. What changed is the range these gates are recorded against and the surface they cover.

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0 on the tree committed this round. packages/contracts/src/stream-candidate.test.ts and its property sibling pin that an explicit null parses while an omitted or undefined fact is rejected and a numeric sentinel is refused; packages/media-engine/src/unknown-media.test.ts and unknown-vs-known.property.test.ts pin that an unstated codec is never certified as supported and remains attemptable as explicitly unverified, that a stated codec the device cannot decode is still rejected, that a height nobody stated cannot exceed maxHeight, that rights are checked before anything unknown can excuse a candidate, and that every unknowable dimension scores zero on a positive weight with no renormalisation, so a fabricated number is neither awarded nor penalised. The acceptance wording this evidence is measured against was rewritten this round on gpt-architect's ruling: it asked which reading of must not PASS was intended, and chose the code's three-state model over rejection.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: Supersedes PL-0205, whose base was false. The implementation predates the claim: the required-and-nullable media facts in domains/playback.ts, the MediaFact vocabulary, and the unknown-aware scoring and ranking in packages/media-engine are all already in committed history. PL-0205 derived its base as the first parent of the first commit touching packages/contracts/src/shared/media-facts.ts, which was wrong because that file was created by PL-AI-0006's module split rather than by the work -- the split moved declarations out of the barrel and its own commit says schema behaviour did not change, so the parent of that creation already contained the semantics. gpt-architect established the true lower bound by reading trees rather than filenames: 4091a2b65b8f187ccb87a04790272007dabd39ea introduced the semantics and names PL-0205 preflight work in its message, and its parent cf2a4583e120151bf16e90d8eb41842cd7329c83 still has mandatory non-null codecs, height and bitrate and none of the unknown-media vocabulary. This base is not merely asserted: before this command ran, the runner verified mechanically that cf2a4583 is an ancestor of HEAD, that its tree contains neither unknownMediaFacts nor MEDIA_FACTS anywhere, and that HEAD contains both, and it would have refused to claim this task at all if any of those failed.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Candidate failover policy
recommended.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel of 1, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** is left wide on purpose -- this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, they share an owner, and narrowing it would buy nothing. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so packages/media-engine/** alone means exactly one of this task, PL-0206 and PL-0205's successor PL-0207 can be active at a time. That is a PATH fact and not a capacity one, and the distinction matters now: claude-media's maxParallel was raised from 1 to 2 in round 40, which changes nothing here because these three still share real files, and was done for PL-0601, whose surface is disjoint from all of them. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0.
recommended.acceptance: Retry and fallback behavior is bounded, deterministic, observable, and testable

recommended.title: Auth integration decision
recommended.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS BOTH NARROWED AND WIDENED, AND THE WIDENING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. As declared, this task reserved docs/**, apps/web/src/** and packages/contracts/** -- all twenty-one documents, the entire web application and the whole contracts package -- for a decision record. Each of those three prefix-contains an active task's write surface, so a P0 that is already finished in the tree could not be claimed by anyone. Worse, and in the opposite direction, packages/auth/** was NOT declared at all, yet nine files there are this task's primary output: a reconcile-existing run would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. Both errors come from declaring a surface by guess before the work exists rather than from reading it afterwards. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and only the control-plane record lags, the same pattern as PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0601. All four acceptance clauses are met: packages/auth exports the seam at . and ./server with better-auth a dependency of that package alone; sessions are database-backed through @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts carries ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES with findSurfaceViolations defaulting unknown plugins to violations; and both better-auth and its adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret, asserted by enabled-surface.test.ts against REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. The decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md, which self-labels Proposed because claude-lead wrote it and is also this task's reviewAgent -- see the reviewAgent change below. TWO HONEST CAVEATS STATED IN THE ADR RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and neither is an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed against a database, because there is no PostgreSQL anywhere in this environment; and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. PROVENANCE: this must be started with --reconcile-existing, not against HEAD. The probe is packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts -- but after the PL-0205 finding, a filename probe is not enough on its own: whoever reconciles it must confirm the candidate base tree contains neither ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES nor WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES anywhere, so a file created by a later move cannot open the range after the behaviour it claims to cover. REVIEWAGENT MOVED FROM claude-lead TO gpt-architect. This task carries a security-review gate on an authentication boundary, and its decision record was written by claude-lead. A reviewer that is also the author is not a reviewer; routing it outward makes the review stricter rather than looser, which is the only direction this may be changed in.
recommended.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

recommended.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
recommended.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
recommended.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

recommended.title: Channel and EPG contracts
recommended.notes: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE, ONLY THE RECORD LAGS -- the fourth task found in this state, after PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0401. packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts is a 592-line contract module whose header names this task, live.test.ts is 686 lines with fast-check property suites, and docs/LIVE_TV.md is a 239-line rewrite around it. All four required contracts exist as real schemas rather than stubs: liveChannelSchema, epgListingSchema, epgWindowSchema and epgScheduleSchema, with epgInstantSchema and the XMLTV timestamp reader beneath them and compareEpgListings, sortEpgListings and sortEpgSchedule for deterministic ordering. THE RIGHTS DIMENSION HOLDS, which matters because this task carries a rights-review gate. A channel's rights basis is REQUIRED and non-nullable, deliberately unlike a title's, and it uses the one shared contentRightsSchema rather than restating the values. No media address or stream URL can appear in a channel or listing: liveChannelSchema declares none, and epgListingSchema is protected three ways -- a PLAYABILITY_BEARING_KEYS list, a CarriesNoPlayability conditional type with a compile-time witness, and .strict() so a feed sending streamUrl is refused rather than silently stripped. rightsBasisForListing refuses a listing that names another channel with a distinguishable reason instead of answering null. The opaque rights reference is not here at all, by design: the live contract carries only the category, and the reference half lives in the provider layer where it is shape-validated and never parsed. logoUrl is the single URL-typed field and is branding rather than media, deliberately absent from PLAYABILITY_BEARING_KEYS. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED FROM packages/contracts/**, which prefix-contained PL-0706's leaf and PL-0207's, to the four files this task actually wrote -- the contract, its suite, its document, and the one assertion in module-boundary.test.ts that had to be retired because it previously asserted src/domains/live.ts must NOT exist. That retirement is this task's edit and is declared rather than left outside every surface. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md is DROPPED: it has no live section, only two bullets under Planned contracts naming /api/v1/live/channels and /api/v1/live/epg, and docs/LIVE_TV.md states the policy that API_CONTRACTS gains live routes when a live route exists. This task defines no HTTP route shapes; those are PL-0602's. Nothing here needs packages/contracts/package.json or index.ts either, because the exports wildcard resolves a new domain module with no metadata edit and the barrel does not re-export live. PREFERREDAGENT MOVED FROM gpt-architect TO claude-media, and this is a correction of fact rather than a reassignment: the implementation in the tree was written in this lane, so recording it as the external agent's would be a false provenance claim. The reviewer stays gpt-architect. PROVENANCE: start with --reconcile-existing. The probe is packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts, and the PL-0205 lesson applies -- confirm the candidate base tree contains no liveChannelSchema or epgListingSchema anywhere before trusting the file's creation date, because a file created by a later refactor opens the range after the behaviour it claims to cover.
recommended.acceptance: Licensed channel, program, schedule, and EPG contracts are typed and documented

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.
